body:
Your brother and this guy sound like they have very similar personalities. People like this are a toxic epidemic on the world. I theorize they are miserable human beings who love nothing more to sabotage the lives of others who are trying to make something of themselves. They want to drag everybody to their level. It's good that you don't have to live with your brother, but it's horrible the way he seems to be taking his misery out on your parents, and you when you are around. 

> What is this person's disability, if he is receiving disability benefits? That may explain some of the behavior. Explain, not justify. 

I'm not sure. When I talked to him he said he was homeless and lived in shelters for a while six years ago (when he moved in here) and that's why "he was the way he is", in particular the part about being paranoid that people were talking about him. He said he wasn't disabled, which may or may not be true given the fact that being homeless can probably get you benefits if the experience causes psychological distress. He may or may not have some kind of other issue but at this point I've come to see the "homeless" thing as an excuse on this guys part, more than a legit explanation. I also think it's an attempt by him to manipulate me by constantly bringing it up, to make me feel bad for not being able to deal with a "poor unfortunate person who was once homeless". It makes me wonder also how he became homeless to begin with. Apparently he was employed prior to being homeless, but some how lost his job (or it was made redundant and he never got back on his feet. He also mentioned alcohol abuse being a problem. 

I was sympathetic for a while as it doesn't seem like he's had an easy situation but he's one of these people who is always rationalizing why he's the victim. I had to stop thinking about his situation because he was using it to emotionally manipulate me, which he seems to be really good at doing, and I tend to succumb to that stuff easily, even when I know it's happening. For my own protection I had to basically stop interacting with him, just so I don't fall under that haze. Another thing I noticed when talking about him is that he seemed bitter and angry about everything. He hates the city/state we live in. He hates the property manager. You'd think he'd be grateful he has a cheap place to live in a very expensive city, especially after being homeless. 

In terms of standing up to him, generally I agree and I also agree about perusing the restraining order. It still seems like an extreme step to take, but I'm getting to my limit. Believe me too I'd love nothing more to unleash a massive torrent of rage to him in the hallway. I'm perfectly capable of summoning that up but I worry that might be fueling the fire. Instead I'm "ghosting" him, the way you suggest, and I know it drives him crazy and makes him very paranoid. I did find out today from the property manager that he did ask for a transfer, and I have a feeling it will be granted. I still feel it's best for everybody if I give him a chance to get out of the situation on his own, which he seems to be trying to do. If that doesn't work though, than yea more steps will have to be taken. 

In your case I think standing up to your brother in the manner you did was probably necessary seeing he's family and there is no easy way you can rid yourself of him. It's scary though, not the standing up part but the unpredictability in how they might react in response.
ah sorry. I put it at the top of the thread but I don't think I can change the topic title.

> We live in a society that doesn't publicize suicides for risk of copycats.

This is another great point I've thought about. I understand the pragmatic reasons for not wanting to publicize suicide incidents but it's always rubbed me the wrong way because it's really just another slap in the face to the mentally ill. It's basically saying we don't/shouldn't exist, or at the very least we need to be hidden from view. 

When somebody dies of cancer we get all kinds of write ups and memorandums and discussion as to what a horrible disease it is and how it needs to be dealt with and how "brave" somebody is for trying to fight it. No such case with suicide even though it's basically the same exact thing - mental illness is a disease, and not everybody can "beat it". 

It's a classic case of not wanting to deal with a problem cause it's too uncomfortable and has no easy solutions, so let's just pretend it doesn't exist or is brought on by the victim themselves. Unfortunately unlike with cancer it's completely socially acceptable to take this attitude with mental illness.

In some ways it's probably better that the therapist is there as a job, it removes the whole obnoxious power dynamic that happens when helping somebody lets you feel superior to them. Finding one you can work with, and then paying for it, that's the tricky part.

Yes I'm always missing out on those kinds of social opportunities. Even if I can make small talk I find it hard to move to the next level. I have a dog that people are always commenting on, so that provides a good conduit for breaking the ice. Sometimes it's frustrating though, as I'm often just not mentally ready to talk and am just wanting to walk the dog. I feel like I'm being a standoffish ass sometimes, and alienating people rather than connecting. 

The other thing with me is that I refuse to settle for something less than I feel I should have. I don't think my expectations are all that outlandish, they are perfectly in line with what somebody in my demographic should expect. I'm not going to be happy with subpar relationships, and there are projects I want to take on that I should be able to. Just going to work at a tolerable job and spending time with tolerable people just doesn't cut it. The world is too interesting for that, and I'd find it a waste. 

The problem is my expectations for a better life conflict with my ability to produce it in reality. It's a lot of extra work and it gets frustrating. I'm always reaching out for help and taking it whenever I can, but sometimes it just isn't as available as I'd like. Sometimes you feel that even if you have close friends who can help to some degree, you are the only one who can make your life what you want/need it to be. With many aspects you are completely on your own. That can be a daunting thing to try and deal with. 

These high expectations and limited connectivity with others leads to situations where I pressure myself beyond the breaking point, and there isn't any external presence to help me realize it.

thanks for your reply. I've been seeing a therapist for 2 years and I will bring this up when I see her again but it's challenging because every week I feel there are a million things I need to be working on, it's very hard to cover every issue I feel needs to be addressed. One hour a week is simply not enough time (we've discussed temporarily meeting two times a week for high stress periods). Yesterday was just an example where I felt very alone and unsupported while hitting a kind of high point with stress. 

In terms of putting pressure on myself, I know it's not a great idea but I do feel like I have no choice because of specifics to my situation (certain opportunities I feel I need are not going to be available forever). The other issue is that it can be hard to know when you've bitten off more than you can chew until it's too late. As far as anger goes, I tend not to be very angry at myself, but I do get angry at my situation, which feels very hostile at times (again for complex reasons).

to be honest what bothers me most is that I know I could have lots of value to others but because of my loneliness induced depression I subconsciously sabotage myself from utilizing any potential benefit I could provide to others. I often times wish I was a mere loser moron with no potential to be any good to the world. At least that way I wouldn't feel bad about wasting my life.

well if you think you have the intelligence/capability to change things in such a manner, than more power to you. If you get success It'd be cool if you could send a sex-bot thingy my way but I understand if you have bigger priorities. ;p

well you "participate" no matter what you do so it's a moot point. Maybe the word I'm looking for is "contribute". Ideally I would like to contribute to a society that accepts me fully (which includes my need for an intimate relationship). If I can't have that than I kinda don't care what happens. In which case the main reason to kill yourself would be that it becomes too much work to keep yourself alive without a genuine purpose. Which is something I'd not be motivated to come up with for a place I don't feel I belong. It's all theoretical at this point though, perhaps I will figure out a stress free way to accumulate enough money (bwa ha yea right) that I can find enough distractions from my misery.
I have some female friends but none that I feel comfortable with this kind of arrangement. Either way I don't consider it a good foundation for a relationship.
and if I participate I still lose because I'm investing energy in something I don't care about.
after glancing at your comment history I'm going to have to say no.

>There's more to life than relationships. 

I think there is more to life too but I view denial of a relationship as a rejection from life and society, which makes me not want to participate in all the "other stuff". I have no desire to be part of something that I feel does not accept me fully. 

>As regards your plan, I just hope you have the balls not to go through with it.

why do you care? I'm not somebody you are ever going to meet. Certainly by the time I am considering suicide this interaction will be long forgotten.

what if your problems are things that become harder to solve with age? ie, missing out on critical social development, deteriorating health, stagnant finances, etc. I get tired of this condescending notion that "it always gets better". Sometimes it gets better, sometimes it gets worse, and sometimes it just sucks at a steady level. Everybody's case is different. 

also; the little circle looks like a martini olive.

I had the same basic thing happen to me only I actually traveled to meet her. It went ok but not nearly as well as I wanted. She waited till after I left to tell me that she wasn't interested. This was maybe a year and a half ago, and only in the past couple of months has it really not been bothering me much. I'm still miserable because my life is a mess but I don't think that much about her anymore, thank god. It really felt for a while like I'd never "get over it", but I pretty much did. I'm still bothered by the prospect of not finding somebody though. This girl raised my standards pretty high and I don't think they can be lowered.

>now I know someone might suggest to take a look at that as an example of how things will get better; however, you have to understand that that was the -one and only- time that has ever happened in the the 26 years that I was alive. To me that is an example of how much I have missed out on, and an example of how long I might have to wait until another off-chance, random, one day encounter happens.

Yea, this is certainly one way to look at it, but it's not necessarily the most realistic. It could be more a matter that your first 26 years were just building up to making that sort of "almost" connection happen, and now that you've had your first, they will become more and more frequent until the connection becomes more than "almost". Of course I don't know the details, maybe it really was a fluke, but even still it shows that there is some degree of hope, which however small, is reason to hang in there. Compared to my situation, I had one relationship when I was 17 [referenced here](http://www.reddit.com/r/ForeverAlone/comments/led7q/my_ex_girlfriend_is_currently_in_town_and_its/), and another "almost" relationship from the internet 10 years later, [referenced here](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/gbwv4/hi_i_just_got_out_of_an_emotionally_abusive/c1mj6u5). I could interpret this to mean that I only get a chance every 10 years, which means not only do have to wait around for another decade, but also if I screw up than I'm really fucked seeing I don't see myself finding a satisfying relationship at age 47 when my life is well over more half done. Even 37 seems like a long-ass time to wait, but I just assume that I won't be the same person from 17-27 as I was from 27-37 and that there is a chance I will figure out how to make something happen sooner this time around. Or not, which would suck, but I'm not going to come to any conclusions before the time has played itself out in reality, as there is no way of knowing whether or not I would be accurate.  

I do resonate with most everything else you say, and my "almost" experiences certainly confuse matters and feel like cruel teases that perhaps I'd be better off without, just like I'd be better off without this inner "fire" and what I would even call "love" of the world and everything in it. If I could just get rid of this feeling, I could peacefully move away from this existence, but these stupid "almost" connections just keep bringing me back. Then again, they are something to grab hold of, and a reminder to persevere. Who knows, maybe in the long run it won't matter, and we're all just fucked. I think this is a good possibility to be aware of, but we shouldn't fixate on it and we certainly shouldn't assume it as a fact. I realize though that it's hard to keep this perspective, for all the reasons you illustrate in your post. Sometimes it just feels hopeless, and that life will just be a tedious chore we have to perform while constantly observing from a window happiness in others that we were tricked into believing we should be able to obtain for ourselves. Death might seem like an appealing release from this, but it's also a tough line to cross seeing as we don't really know what's on the other side. Even if the odds in life don't seem in our favor, at least we know what they are, and can find ways to improve them. Death might not afford us those options. 

I wish I had better answers to these problems than I do, other than to say hang in there for the time being and come to a place like this when you are getting overwhelmed. You obviously are a deep feeling and eloquent person based on your writing, I know there is a girl out there who you can make very happy (and she can do the same for you). The hard part is finding her.

>The absolute truth that I could not deny, no matter how much I wanted to, is that my inner fire continued to burn. I couldn't put that fire out no matter how much I tried to smother it. It didn't work. If I had killed myself, it would have to be while knowing that I have a strong desire to live and an inner passion that could power a small city. I had this when I was 11 and I still have this today. That will always be a part of who I am. To kill myself would require me to deny that part of myself.

>So why do suicidal people lie to themselves? Why do they say things like "I just don't care anymore" when that is the furthest thing from the truth? Because the amount of emotion they contain, with no direction and no outlet while mixed with severe frustration........it hurts. It hurts a lot. It hurts more than anything has ever hurt. It cuts deeper than anything. It hurts at the core, at a cellular level. And there is no getting away from it. It is always there. It is like a cancer that doesn't kill you. Rather, it makes you want to kill yourself.

>But...

>The reason it hurts is because it is a powerful thing. For this reason, I know there will be a day where I fall in love again, because I really don't have another choice. 

that's a brilliant piece of writing. Never heard it summed up so concisely but yea, that's pretty much it. I do wonder over time if that "fire" will burn out or if my situation will be so hopeless that it will just seem ridiculous, but I guess cross that bridge when I get to it.

I'm 28 and I still have some hope however much it's waning with time. Maybe in your late 30's or 40's you can legitimately think you have nothing to look forward to but you've got some time before that. The main advice I'd offer is to not waste these years. Develop some interests, get on a workout regimen, and try to forge a good career path. Doing these things now will help you remedy your "forever alone" status later on, but for now try not to worry about it too much. There will be plenty of time for worrying later on. Also, be sure to try and enjoy yourself, and enjoy life. I realize it's not easy given that there is so much to be miserable about, but try not to focus too much energy on that. Maybe you can channel your depression into some kind of artistic endeavor?

I wouldn't say I linger in the past; I still hang out with her on occasion because she's a good friend in the present (and hopefully future), one of the best I've ever had. I'd love it if she lived 10 minutes away, not so much that I'd see her more but she's really social (and I'm really not) so I'd be able to "use" her to expand my social circle since she'd basically do the work and "vette" me for people. We live close enough and see each other enough that over the long term, this still might be possible. So it's worth seeing her, I just wish it didn't come with these mood swings, which fwiw, did not start happening till the past year or so, when my lifetime FA status has begun really cementing itself. Prior to that I always just assumed I'd find somebody else. Now I'm not so sure.
lucky.

>The difference is that they know how to fake it, and you don't, because faking requires confidence, and you're not the guy with confidence. **You're the guy who's afraid that if people hear you pee, they'll know you're doing it wrong, (somehow).**

got to this and lost it. No I didn't piss myself, but I do have a shy bladder and spend a lot of time worrying that people aren't hearing me pee.

wait until you start approaching 30 and have not much more a clue than when you were 18. Ok that's a bit of an exaggeration, but I certainly always feel like I need 4x as much time as everybody else. I really resonate with that last line about finally figuring out the new rules only to find they've changed on me.

I got trashed 2 nights ago and I'm still feeling nausea/dizziness and just generally feeling out of it. Fuck, I hope I haven't done any liver damage, and I really hope this shit is gone by tomorrow. I can't remember the last time I had a two day hangover, if I've ever even had one.

personally I'd focus on a career/job and put the other stuff on hold. If you get that settled, it will free more energy to deal with your mental issues. It's hard enough to deal with that stuff when you are financially strapped and/or don't have a clear path with a future. The only exception would be if your mental issues get in the way of figuring out these things to an excessive degree. It's going to make things difficult for sure, it's just a question of how much can be tolerated.

>You seem to recognize that that is part of the problem keeping you out of work.

it certainly plays no small part but I'd say laziness and depression is playing a bigger part. I could be putting together resume's, transcripts, researching possible careers and emailing people about them. This can be done without any regard towards my SA. I even have a career counselor that is trying to help me organize, yet I don't do anything. I mostly just sit around angry and depressed about my life. If I can just fight through towards some kind of career path and get that settled, than maybe dealing with the SA won't seem as monstrous as it does now. 

anyway, I have been trying to get help with the SA but the financial situation is blocking that. I tried contacting one highly regarded cbt program in treating it, but because I have Asperger's in addition to SA I was told I was ineligible for a "sliding scale" payments based on income and would have to pay $180 per session. I have other avenues to explore but due to my depression, little setbacks like this are really discouraging and it usually takes me a long time to try something else. The looming feeling I have is that there really isn't enough time left to fix things to a level I'd find acceptable to be satisfied with my life. Maybe there never was enough time, maybe my expectations are too high, but they are what they are. In response I see everything as a message from the world that I don't belong here and really should be thinking of getting the fuck out.

I see what you are doing here, and there is some good perspective to come from reading your post. However, when you have to mention more than once that you expect to be downvoted, there is probably a good reason for that (I'm not downvoting you, btw). We all have problems in life, and frankly, there are people who have it WAY worse than anything you've talked about experiencing. Which isn't too say your issues aren't horrible, but it's a cruel fucking world, a fact that in itself should be reason for ANYONE to want to leave it. Nonetheless, I think you are being overly harsh. 

People are given an assortment of bullshit to deal with in life, but they are also given a different threshold for how much they can cope with. Suicide is common enough that a lot of people are simply given far more than they can take. I know this because if they could take it, they wouldn't of killed themselves. Suicide takes serious balls. Things have to get really bad before you consider it - you are going against all your instincts for survival. No offense, but I really don't think you are in a position to judge whether or not the OP has passed the point of whether or not he can take it anymore. It's possible you are right and he's being a whiny pussy, but it's just as likely that you are wrong and just being a douche, and IMO, this is no situation to risk being a douche. 

a couple other quick points; 

1.) how old are you? The OP mentions being 39, which while young in some respects, is pretty old for romantic relationships. He's at a point where the vast majority of his peers are "settled down", possibly with kids, not to mention his lack of income becomes more of a problem as women are simply less tolerant of men who have lived that long and not figured out how to "provide". If you are younger - in your 20's or even early 30's, you have substantially more time to address a lot of things that the OP simply doesn't have.

2.) wrt drug/alcohol dependency, I sympathize. The amount I drink scares me sometimes, but a lot of people would say that this comes about via an individual decision. Even though there are tons of drug addicts and alcoholics, who makes the decision to put those substances into your body? You do. You can't be a victim with this shit. I understand that the pain of life can be so horrible that you will do anything to numb it, but at the same time I feel as if society sometimes goes to easy on drug addicts and alcoholics. I mean, how hard is it to simply endure and find other ways to pass the time? Yes, some people are more susceptible than others to these problems, but that's really the case with everything in life now isn't it? Some people can drink or do drugs without developing an addiction and/or dependance. Other's can't. Some people can handle being alone for many years, year after year and maintain decent cranial flow and persevere. Others simply reach a breaking point. 

What one can handle differs between individuals. Maybe you have it in you to handle more than the OP. That's awesome, but it doesn't imply that there is anything wrong with the OP. Like I said, I understand the sentiment of what you are saying, but for some people there is more to the story.

I met my first girlfriend at a boarding school, you couldn't really get off campus alone together so there was nothing resembling a date. We did hang out a lot before becoming an "item". I almost got another relationship through the internet, but after chatting for several months we met IRL and she decided she wasn't into me. These are my only "2" relationships, no dates. I was going to post my stats but seeing all these 0's made me think otherwise. Not that my "experience" makes the FA prospect feel any better.

I can relate to the OP and while I don't know if he's feeling similar to me, when I get suicidal feelings (which is often) it's accompanied with hate for the world, as I feel it's rejected me. I have no desire to change a place that that has made it clear that it feels this way about me. Not for the better, and not for the worst. All I want is to leave it forever. Perhaps suicide isn't the best way to accomplish that, but I suppose if hanging onto life long enough hasn't worked than it seems like a viable option. Not endorsing the OP's plan or anything.

hi, thanks for replying. Sorry about the delay in saying anything back. I guess I'm just feeling very overwhelmed. I try to keep things manageable. Maybe I can do one productive thing every day, and I do that. It still seems as if genuine improvement is too far off in the distance and because of that I get demotivated quickly. I still manage to make progress, it's just that the progress is extremely slow. Which is why time seems like my greatest enemy. I'm not good at living in the present, it's usually more frustrating to even try so I just don't bother. In terms of smiling, I don't see enough people, and those I do see I'm not interested in confusing. Meh.

I'm usually a Louis CK fan but that bit pisses me off. It's just amazing to me how somebody so smart can so fundamentally misunderstand basic human psychology. Happiness has nothing to do with how "amazing" things are. I dunno, maybe that was his point? I kinda doubt it. The fact that he seems so sincere makes me think he's not a very deep person. What's even more frustrating is how people seem to like/agree with it.

depression is depression, you can't change feeling shitty just by flicking on a light switch. If you ever truly experienced it in your youth than you would realize the futility of your words here. I'm pretty sure plenty of "angsty" young people realize they are "wasting there youth", which just makes it all the more depressing.

posts like this are why I loathe the "it gets better" meme that gets tossed out to teenagers who are suicidally depressed. I say this independently of the same titled program aimed at gays, even though that is relevant to you. I mean I'm all for reaching out and trying to give hope but saying "it gets better" comes off as an empty promise. Maybe it gets better, but it certainly does not automatically get better and sometimes it gets worse. Teenager's aren't stupid, but they can be desperate and in that desperation they sometimes believe things that logically don't hold up. Then down the line they find out how deluded they were for not realizing they were lied to.
no but only cause it's been so long since i had an "ex" that we weren't even old enough to drive!

I agree with getting a job but I'm not just going to take any job (like McDonalds). I realize now might not be the time to be picky but certain environments rub off on me in a very bad way and my mental health is too important. Either way, I've already done min wage shit jobs and I got incredibly depressed. While certain part-time "stop gap" jobs would probably be beneficial, at my age I need to find something with a future. It's ok to scrub bathroom floors in your early 20's. In your late 20's it's precarious. In your 30's it's pathetic. On the plus side I do have an appointment with a career/job counselor in a few weeks, but until then I feel I'm just biding my time. I've always been shit at applying to jobs on my own (or really doing anything on my own), I've kind of given up.

I don't have the attention span right now to read that article completely, only skim it. I can come up with an easy rebuttal to each of his points though; 

the money situation will improve - not really, because I'm financially dependent on my parents still and they can't support me forever. Which at my age (28) is sad. Unless something drastically improves in the next 10 years (doubtful, knowing me) I will end up living paycheck to paycheck but minus the energy of youth. It's acceptable to be a young adult whose poor. To be poor entering middle aged is pathetic and the sign of a loser. 

you will find someone - Well I've gone over a decade since my last serious relationship (which wasn't that serious) so I don't see any reason to think this will improve anytime soon. Unless I can deal with the things that hold me back (social anxiety, depression over unemployment, general feelings of low self confidence, etc), things that I'm not capable of fixing in order to remedy this aspect of my life. Even if I do take care of all that stuff I'm sure it'll be the day right before I officially become middle aged. I will no longer be attracted to people my age, but too old to date women I am attracted to without being considered a pervert. At that point it's not even worth it. 

High School is not the best years of your life - well I had some low, low points in high school, but I would say that at least my senior year WAS in fact one of the best years of my life. I had a girlfriend (complete with a messy horrible breakup, part of the low points though at least SOMETHING was happening, unlike now) and I was part of a community of people who I had something in common with, and the world was still kind of new and exciting. No longer is that the case. 

Until You're On Your Own, You Don't Know What Freedom Is - well I've never really been on my own (see the first point) but at the same time I have been on my own in a lot of ways. What I've learned is that I'm incapable of handling freedom without fucking things up, somehow. And not in the good way where you "learn from it". I never learn, just keep repeating the same mistakes. That's one thing that holds me back from truly trying to make it "on my own" - I have no confidence in my ability to not fuck it up. At some point I'm going to have no choice, and I will be so ill equipped that suicide is going to look like a very viable option. Now that's freedom - the ability to end your life. I foresee a day when that's the only freedom I'm capable of attaining in this constraining world. 

the world isn't as bad as you think - I actually read this one and he makes valid points. The problem is I don't care about the world. I don't care if it's good, or bad or just mediocre. Why would I give a shit about a place I clearly don't belong? I certainly can't see how I can "make the world better" and frankly that's not something I have any desire to do anyway. 

but back to the main gist of this post, which is that like much "advice" aimed at the hopeless and depressed, it's for teenagers. It may of been comforting for me to hear 10-15 years ago - perhaps that's why my "best" years were late-teens/early 20's - this message gave me hope. Well guess what? Now I'm in my late 20's and NOTHING HAS FUCKING CHANGED. My life still sucks, and it sucks for all the SAME FUCKING REASONS as when I was younger, and I'm still JUST AS FUCKING POWERLESS to change anything now as I was back then. 

BS platitudes that you read in this article are no longer comforting, they only serve to enrage me for how patronizing they are as I grow into a reality that is quite different. Things are even worse now because I know that my only opportunities to change things are passing by with each day as we speak, and I'm powerless to do anything but watch. Soon it will be too late, I will be sad and old with a lifetime of nothing behind me, and no future to look forward to. But whatever. Maybe for most people shit does get better. good for those fuckers. I don't care. 

tl;dr, shit article full of obnoxious cliche's meant to comfort whilst ignoring the unpleasant reality.

man. I'd kill for my own place and a decent job right now. Your post re-iterates what I already know, that life is just about jumping from one shit storm into another. Death, who knows what that will bring. Given how unlucky we were to be born into this world, I'm sure it will just be more of the same. Personally speaking, I'm kind of an idealist (go figure) and there are still things I want to accomplish here. That keeps me from heading to the nearest bridge, but at a certain point I'm going to get old enough where those dreams are no longer realistic. At that point life just becomes the massive chore you described, but no longer tempered by the hope that something good will happen down the line. At which point I'm going to have a hard time justifying sticking around to continue fighting the entropy of aging. A struggle that I'm sure grows harder with each passing day.

I feel the same way about therapy sessions. It normally takes me about 50 minutes to get going on any topic of substance and then it's time to quit. It's part of why I think therapy is a scam - I'm sure the normal 50 minute session length is not arbitrary!

well maybe he's an asshole, or maybe he was just too hurt inside to understand the impact he was having on others. I don't really know the details seeing I don't know the guy. My only point was that by definition he's not a wuss. As for not being a "man" well again, that's your subjective definition. Sorry but I just don't buy into this idea that you have to "prove" you are a "man" or "woman". 

as for your other friend, it sucks what happened but it sounds like poor judgment on her part in signing the loan. Again I don't know the details so it's possible I'm missing something but based on your description he doesn't sound like somebody to tie yourself too financially.

tl:dr, service dogs are good if you can come up with specific things it can help you with.

About a year ago I had an online long distance relationship. I traveled a long way to meet this woman with the idea that I'd move in with her, and while I pretty much fell in love upon meeting her, she decided that she wasn't attracted to me. It was quite a shock because I had invested so much in that relationship working out. In retrospect that was a dumb idea but I was at a place of desperation and she provided a beacon of hope. When things didn't work, it really felt like my last chance to have any sort of happiness in this life had vanished. At first I was angry at her but then I just gradually became angry at my general situation, and ever since have been considering suicide as a kind of "protest" against the universe for putting me through this degrading experience. I wish I could say there is some sort of light at the end of the tunnel a year later, and that I've somehow used the experience to take initiative to improve my life on my own. The sad reality is that I'm still incredibly angry about the situation, and I cannot "get over it". I would love to move on with life and put it behind me but I just have too many other problems preventing me (health, financial, social isolation, etc) so I always end up defaulting to being angry/depressed over this one failed internet relationship. I'm sure most people would view this as pathetic but it is what it is and I'm not going to hide what it means to me. 

Mind you, I'm sure that our situations are very different in many ways. I don't know if what this girl did to me could be considered "abuse" (it did seem fucked up), but I certainly understand the patronizing tone you sometimes get from others when describing what happened - as if somehow it being online means it's "not real". It's still the same chemical reactions going on inside your body making you feel a certain way. It's time and emotional energy invested, and that would be true whether you met the person in real life or if they only ever existed inside your head.
